page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.8 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the n2-highcpu-16 in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 14867.36, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 7164.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1408.59 and a bzip3 single-threaded decompression rate of 8.77 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 82.43 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 42.68 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which limits its utility for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. However, it supports advanced vector instructions like AVX-512, which assists in specific mathematical workloads. It achieves 14.12 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 12.3 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. This server is suited for compute-bound workloads with low memory footprints, such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight text or image processing.
